application: PDT (Police Digital Trunking) — Chinese public safety digital radio standard, used by Chinese police (Gong An), fire, and emergency services. This is China's equivalent of TETRA but uses a different standard.

notes: CRITICAL: China does NOT use TETRA in the 380-395 MHz band like Europe. Instead, China uses PDT (Police Digital Trunking) in 350-370 MHz. PDT was developed by Hytera and standardized by the Chinese Ministry of Public Security. PDT is technically similar to DMR but with Chinese-specific features including built-in encryption, GPS, and dispatching. Over 1 million PDT terminals deployed in China as of 2020.

application: Airwave network uplink — UK emergency services TETRA. Used by all 43 police forces in England and Wales, Police Scotland, PSNI, all fire and rescue services, ambulance services, and other Category 1/2 responders. Operated by Airwave Solutions (Motorola Solutions subsidiary, formerly O2 Airwave).
typical_devices: Sepura STP9000 series, Sepura SC20/SC21 (Sepura is UK-based), Motorola Solutions MTP850/MTP3250 TETRA, Hytera PD985 (TETRA variant)
regulatory_ref: Ofcom, ECC/DEC/(08)05, Airwave Solutions PMSE licence, Home Office Emergency Services Network (ESN) programme (replacement planned)
notes: Airwave is one of the largest TETRA networks globally with ~3,700 base stations covering 99% of UK landmass. Originally planned for replacement by ESN (4G-based Emergency Services Network on EE/BT network) but ESN has been delayed repeatedly. Airwave contract extended to at least 2029. Over 300,000 TETRA terminals in UK.

application: BOS-Digitalfunk (BOSnet) uplink — German emergency services TETRA network. Used by Polizei (all 16 Lander), Feuerwehr, Rettungsdienst, THW, Bundespolizei, Zoll. Operated by BDBOS (Bundesanstalt fur den Digitalfunk der Behorden und Organisationen mit Sicherheitsaufgaben).
typical_devices: Sepura STP9000/SC20, Motorola Solutions MTP6650 TETRA, Hytera PT580H Plus (BOS-certified), Airbus THR880i (BOS version)
modulation: TETRA (pi/4 DQPSK), 25 kHz, 4-slot TDMA, end-to-end encryption (E2EE)
regulatory_ref: BNetzA Frequenzplan, BDBOS Authorisation, ECC/DEC/(08)05, BOS-Funkrichtlinie (TR BOS)
notes: BOSnet is one of the world's largest TETRA networks with ~4,900 base stations (as of 2024). Built by Motorola Solutions (formerly EADS/Cassidian). Uses TETRA with E2EE. Coverage: >99% population. Network declared operationally complete in 2016. Over 1 million BOS radio users in Germany.

application: SIRDEE (Sistema de Radiocomunicaciones Digitales de Emergencia del Estado) uplink — Spanish national emergency services TETRA network. Used by Guardia Civil, Policia Nacional, CNP, bomberos, SAMUR/061 emergency medical. Additionally, autonomous communities operate regional networks: RESCAT (Catalonia), SOS-Deiak (Basque Country), COMDES (Valenciana).
typical_devices: Sepura STP8000/9000 series, Motorola Solutions MTP850/MTP3250, Teltronic TETRA base stations (Teltronic is a Spanish company, now Sepura/Hytera)
regulatory_ref: CNAF nota UN-77, ECC/DEC/(08)05, Min. del Interior / SETSI
notes: SIRDEE was deployed starting 2004 by the Spanish Interior Ministry. Teltronic (now owned by Hytera via Sepura) is based in Zaragoza, Spain and is a significant TETRA infrastructure manufacturer. Spain also has multiple autonomous community TETRA networks operating in the same band.

application: Italian emergency services TETRA uplink. Carabinieri, Polizia di Stato, Vigili del Fuoco, and 118 (emergency medical) use TETRA networks. Italy has a fragmented TETRA deployment with multiple provincial and regional networks rather than a single national network.
typical_devices: Motorola Solutions MTP850/MTP3250, Sepura STP8000/9000, Hytera TETRA terminals
notes: Italy's TETRA deployment is less centralized than France/UK/Germany. Multiple provincial networks exist. Some forces still use legacy analog systems alongside TETRA. National interoperability remains a challenge.

application: Polycom network uplink — Swiss emergency services TETRA/TETRAPOL network. Used by cantonal police, fire, ambulance, border guard (GWK), Swiss Army (civil protection role). Switzerland uses TETRAPOL (not TETRA) — a competing French-origin standard by Airbus (formerly EADS/Matra).
typical_devices: Airbus TETRAPOL TPH900 handheld, Airbus TMR880i mobile, Airbus TETRAPOL infrastructure (DXT3p switches)
modulation: TETRAPOL (GMSK modulation, 10 kHz or 12.5 kHz channel spacing, FDMA not TDMA)
regulatory_ref: BAKOM Frequenzzuweisungsplan, BABS (Bundesamt fur Bevolkerungsschutz) Polycom programme, ECC/DEC/(08)05
notes: IMPORTANT: Switzerland uses TETRAPOL, NOT TETRA, for its Polycom emergency services network. TETRAPOL is an FDMA system (vs TETRA's TDMA). TETRAPOL was also used in France (Gendarmerie RUBIS network) before migration to TETRA INPT. Czech Republic also uses TETRAPOL. Channel spacing is 12.5 kHz (TETRAPOL) vs 25 kHz (TETRA).

application: Federal Government exclusive — Used by federal agencies (DoD, DHS, FBI, DEA, Secret Service, etc.) for UHF LOS communications. This is NOT TETRA — US does not use TETRA in this band. US public safety uses VHF/UHF P25 (APCO-25) on other frequencies (700/800 MHz, 136-174 MHz, 406-470 MHz).
typical_devices: Harris XG-100P (P25 multiband), Motorola Solutions APX8000 (P25 but on other bands), various federal agency UHF LMR radios
modulation: FM narrowband (12.5 kHz), some P25 Phase I (C4FM), legacy FM wideband (25 kHz)
power_limit: Per NTIA authorization — typically up to 50W for mobile stations
regulatory_ref: NTIA Manual Chapter 4, 47 CFR 2.106 footnotes G27/G30, IRAC (Interdepartment Radio Advisory Committee) coordination
notes: CRITICAL CORRECTION: The US does NOT use TETRA in 380-400 MHz. This entire band (380-400 MHz) is Federal Government exclusive, managed by NTIA (not FCC). US public safety uses P25 (APCO Project 25) on 700 MHz (764-776/794-806 MHz), 800 MHz (806-824/851-869 MHz), VHF, and UHF bands — NOT 380-400 MHz TETRA.

application: Chinese government/military use. China does NOT use TETRA in 380-385 MHz. Chinese public safety uses PDT (Police Digital Trunking) in 350-370 MHz instead. This band may be used for PLA or paramilitary (PAP) communications.
typical_devices: PLA/PAP standard radios, some Hytera DMR/PDT terminals
modulation: FM, DMR, proprietary Chinese military waveforms
regulatory_ref: MIIT Radio Regulations, PLA General Staff Department frequency management
notes: CRITICAL: China does NOT use TETRA for public safety. Chinese police use PDT standard in 350-370 MHz. The 380-400 MHz band in China is primarily military/government, not PPDR TETRA as in Europe.

application: Russian government/military/security services. Russia has limited TETRA deployments for some MVD and emergency services but NOT in a unified national network like Europe. Some cities have TETRA pilot networks. Primary use remains military.
typical_devices: Limited TETRA: Sepura, Motorola Solutions TETRA terminals in some city networks; Military: Russian standard UHF radios
notes: Russia does not have a national TETRA PPDR network comparable to European countries. Some major cities (Moscow, St. Petersburg, Sochi) have localized TETRA deployments for police and emergency services, but coverage is not nationwide. The Russian emergency services also use their own digital standards and APCO-25 variant equipment.

application: Extended PPDR uplink and military sharing band. In France, this sub-band provides additional capacity for INPT TETRA and allows military/civil shared use. Used for interoperability between military and civilian emergency services during joint operations (e.g., Sentinelle, Vigipirate).
typical_devices: Same TETRA terminals as 380-385 MHz band (Airbus THR880i, Sepura STP9000, Motorola MTP6550)
power_limit: Same as PPDR: mobile 1-3W, BS up to 25W
regulatory_ref: ANFR TNRBF, ECC/DEC/(08)05 extended PPDR provisions, ARCEP
notes: 385-390 MHz is designated for extended PPDR and civil/military sharing in CEPT countries. Some countries use it for additional TETRA capacity; others retain it for military use. France uses it for both.

application: Extended PPDR uplink; shared with MoD. Airwave network can use extended capacity in this sub-band.
typical_devices: Airwave TETRA terminals (same as 380-385)
notes: Shared civil PPDR/military. MoD retains priority access rights.

application: Extended BOS-Digitalfunk uplink capacity; shared with Bundeswehr
typical_devices: BOSnet TETRA terminals (same as 380-385)
notes: Shared BOS/Bundeswehr. Additional TETRA carriers available for high-demand events.

application: Federal Government exclusive — continuation of federal UHF LMR. Same agencies and use as 380-385 MHz.
typical_devices: Federal agency UHF LMR radios
notes: Federal exclusive. No TETRA. No civilian access.

application: Extended SIRDEE TETRA capacity; shared with Fuerzas Armadas
typical_devices: SIRDEE TETRA terminals
notes: Extended PPDR / military sharing.

application: Extended TETRA capacity; military sharing; Carabinieri and Polizia additional channels
typical_devices: TETRA terminals (same as 380-385)
notes: Extended PPDR / military sharing.

application: Extended Polycom (TETRAPOL) capacity; shared with Swiss Armed Forces
typical_devices: Airbus TETRAPOL TPH900 (same as 380-385)
notes: Extended PPDR / military sharing. Switzerland uses TETRAPOL, not TETRA.

application: Government/military. Not TETRA. China's public safety operates PDT in 350-370 MHz.
typical_devices: Military/government radios
notes: Not TETRA. Chinese public safety uses PDT at 350-370 MHz.

application: Government/military. Limited TETRA for some city emergency networks.
typical_devices: Military radios; limited TETRA terminals in select cities
notes: Primarily military. Limited localized TETRA deployments.

application: INPT TETRA network downlink (base station transmit). Paired with 380-385 MHz uplink. Base stations transmit to all INPT user terminals (Police, Gendarmerie, Pompiers, SAMU).
typical_devices: Airbus TETRA base stations (TBS series), Motorola Solutions TETRA infrastructure (DIMETRA IP), Sepura STP9000/SC20 (receive)
power_limit: Base station: 5-25W per carrier (typical 10W urban, 25W rural); mobile receive sensitivity: -112 dBm (TETRA standard)
regulatory_ref: ARCEP, ECC/DEC/(08)05, ETSI EN 300 392-2, ANFR TNRBF
notes: 390-395 MHz is the base station transmit (downlink) band, FDD paired with 380-385 MHz uplink with 10 MHz duplex spacing. Maximum 200 x 25 kHz channels available in the 5 MHz bandwidth.

application: Airwave TETRA network downlink. Base stations transmit to all Airwave user terminals. Paired with 380-385 MHz uplink.
typical_devices: Motorola Solutions DIMETRA IP infrastructure, Sepura STP9000/SC20/SC21 (receive), Motorola MTP3250 (receive)
notes: Airwave downlink. 10 MHz duplex spacing. ~3,700 base stations nationwide.

application: BOSnet (BOS-Digitalfunk) TETRA downlink. Base stations transmit to all BOS user terminals. Paired with 380-385 MHz uplink.
typical_devices: Motorola Solutions DIMETRA Express/IP infrastructure, Sepura STP9000/SC20 (receive), Hytera PT580H Plus (receive)
notes: BOSnet downlink. ~4,900 base stations. E2EE (end-to-end encryption) deployed across the network.

application: SIRDEE TETRA downlink. Paired with 380-385 MHz uplink.
typical_devices: Teltronic TETRA base stations, Sepura/Motorola terminals (receive)
notes: SIRDEE downlink.

application: Italian TETRA network downlink. Paired with 380-385 MHz uplink.
typical_devices: Various TETRA infrastructure and terminals
notes: Italian TETRA downlink. Fragmented deployment across provinces.

application: Polycom TETRAPOL network downlink. Paired with 380-385 MHz uplink.
typical_devices: Airbus TETRAPOL base stations (DXT3p), TPH900 (receive)
notes: Polycom downlink. TETRAPOL (FDMA), not TETRA (TDMA).

application: Federal Government exclusive — federal UHF LMR. NOT TETRA.

notes: Federal exclusive. NOT TETRA. US uses P25 on 700/800 MHz for public safety.

notes: Extended PPDR downlink. Available for emergency services overflow during major incidents. Military retains right of way.

application: RNSS (radionavigation-satellite) satellite system (search and rescue); also upper boundary of federal UHF band. 399.9-400.05 MHz is allocated to Radionavigation-Satellite worldwide.
typical_devices: Argos PTT transmitters, satellite RNSS receivers
notes: 399.9-400.05 MHz is a worldwide allocation for radionavigation-satellite (downlink). This serves as a transition between the military UHF band (225-400 MHz) and the meteorological/space research bands above 400 MHz. [FACTCHECK CORRECTION: COSPAS-SARSAT emergency beacons transmit at 406.0-406.1 MHz, NOT 399.9 MHz. The 399.9-400.05 MHz allocation is for RNSS downlinks (Argos system).]
